lessons.title: Right Circular Cones

activities.prompt: Have you ever wondered what happens when we unroll a cone?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet a right circular cone
activities.body: A right-angled triangle has two sides meeting at a right angle. Rotate it about one of these sides. This forms a right circular cone. Its slant length, height and base radius satisfy l² = h² + r². Opening the curved surface gives a sector of a circle. The curved surface area is πrl. The total surface area is πrl + πr². Its volume is one-third of its base area multiplied by its height.
keyPoints: Rotating a right-angled triangle forms a right circular cone.
The slant length, height and radius satisfy l² = h² + r².
A cone has special formulas for surface area and volume.
activities.explanation: Remember the shape, its formulas and its special one-third volume.

activities.title: Show the one-third rule

tasks.say: Shade 1 part in a bar of 3 equal parts.
tasks.then: You have shown one-third of the bar.

tasks.say: Shade 2 parts in a bar of 6 equal parts.
tasks.then: You have shown the same one-third fraction.

tasks.say: Shade 3 parts in a bar of 9 equal parts.
tasks.then: You have shown one-third in another way.

activities.takeaway: A cone has one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height, so three cones fill the cylinder.
activities.explanation: A cone has one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and height, so three cones fill the cylinder.

activities.prompt: A shop makes cone-shaped party hats without bases. How can the worker find the amount of paper needed?
steps: The hat has a curved surface, because it has no flat base.
The curved surface area of a cone is πrl, because this measures the curved part.
The radius r measures the hat’s opening, while l measures its slant side.
So the worker needs πrl square units of paper for the whole hat.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Make a cone
activities.prompt: How can you make a right circular cone?
options: Slide a right triangle across one leg.
Rotate a right triangle about one leg.
Roll a right triangle into a flat circle.
Keep a right triangle completely still.
activities.explanation: Rotating a right-angled triangle about one leg forms a right circular cone.

activities.title: Complete the formula
activities.prompt: A cone obeys l² = h² + ______.
activities.hint: Use the symbol for the base radius.
activities.explanation: The slant length, height and base radius satisfy l² = h² + r².

activities.title: Match measurements and symbols
activities.prompt: Match each cone measurement with its symbol.
activities.explanation: In l² = h² + r², l means slant length, h means height and r means radius.

activities.title: Compare the volumes
activities.prompt: A cone and cylinder have the same base radius and height. What is true?
options: The cone has one-third of the cylinder’s volume.
The cone and cylinder have equal volumes.
The cone has more volume than the cylinder.
The cylinder has one-third of the cone’s volume.
activities.explanation: The cone has one-third of the cylinder’s volume. Three conefuls of salt fill the cylinder. The same clay can make exactly three matching cones.

activities.title: Choose the surface formula

πr² + πrl gives the curved area
πrl + πh² gives the total area
πr² − πrl gives the total area
activities.explanation: The total surface area is πrl + πr². The curved surface area alone is πrl.

activities.title: See how the cone develops
activities.prompt: Put these actions in the correct order.

Reveal a sector of a circle.
activities.explanation: Rotating the triangle makes the cone. Unrolling its curved surface reveals a circular sector.

activities.prompt: At the bus park, a cylindrical tank has the same base radius 9 cm and height 4 cm as a cone. How many conefuls of water fill the tank?
activities.explanation: The cone and cylinder have the same base radius 9 cm and height 4 cm. For equal radius and height, the cylinder has three times the cone's volume. Therefore three conefuls fill the tank, so the answer is 3 conefuls.
steps: The cone and cylinder have the same base radius 9 cm and height 4 cm.

Therefore three conefuls fill the tank, so the answer is 3 conefuls.
activities.hint: Compare the volumes when the radius and height are the same.

why.πr², because only the circular base need: The child wrongly counts a base that the hat does not have.
why.πrl + πr², because the hat also includes: The child adds a base area even though no base is present.
why.πrl - πr², because the base area must be: The child thinks a base must be removed from the curved area.

activities.prompt: Two cones have the same radius. One has a greater height. What happens to its slant length?
options: It increases, because the larger height makes l² greater.
It decreases, because the larger height makes l² smaller.
It stays equal, because the unchanged radius fixes l.
It stays equal, because the changed height has no effect.

why.It decreases, because the larger height: The child subtracts r² instead of adding it in the relation.
why.It stays equal, because the unchanged ra: The child wrongly thinks the unchanged radius fixes slant length.
why.It stays equal, because the changed heig: The child wrongly thinks a changed height cannot change slant length.

activities.explanation: At fixed radius, greater height makes l² greater, so l grows.

Two-thirds of the cylinder remains empty.
One-half of the cylinder remains empty.
The whole cylinder remains empty.

why.Two-thirds of the cylinder remains empty: The child swaps the empty fraction with the filled fraction.
The child divides the cylinder into two equal parts, not three.
The child ignores the two conefuls already poured into the cylinder.

activities.explanation: Two of three conefuls are used, so one-third remains empty.

activities.prompt: A child says an opened cone must be a complete circle. Why is that claim flawed?
options: A sector appears, because the cone opens into part of a circle.
A triangle appears, because the cone has one pointed top.
A rectangle appears, because the cone has straight vertical sides.
A full circle appears, because every cone uses all the paper.

why.A triangle appears, because the cone has: The child confuses the cone’s pointed side with its opened surface.
why.A rectangle appears, because the cone ha: The child thinks the cone’s straight side unfolds into a rectangle.
why.A full circle appears, because every con: The child wrongly assumes the curved surface uses one complete circle.

activities.explanation: It opens as a sector, so it cannot be a complete circle.

activities.title: Parts of a Pyramid
activities.body: A pyramid has a flat base and one top point called the apex. Its base may be triangular, square, or another closed shape. Every base point joins the apex in a different plane. Its outside surface consists of polygonal faces. To find surface area, add these faces. To find volume, use the base area and height. This method works for any flat base.
keyPoints: The base may be triangular, square, or another closed shape.
Every base point joins one apex in a different plane.
Surface area comes from polygonal faces; volume uses base area and height.
activities.explanation: Pyramids have one apex, a closed base, polygonal faces, and a clear volume rule.

activities.prompt: A square-based pyramid has a base area of 15 cm² and a height of 3 cm. What is its volume in cm³?
steps: The base area is 15 cm² and the height is 3 cm.
Multiply them to get 45 cm³.
A pyramid's volume is one-third of the product of its base area and height, so divide 45 by three.
The volume is 15 cm³.

lessons.title: Spheres and Hemispheres

activities.prompt: What makes a sphere so much more than a circle?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Meet Spheres and Hemispheres
activities.body: A sphere is the three-dimensional form of a circle. All its points sit the same distance r from its centre. A hemisphere is one equal half of a sphere. It has a curved surface and a circular base. You will compare the surface areas and volumes of these shapes.
keyPoints: A sphere is the 3D equivalent of a circle.
A hemisphere has one curved surface and one circular base.
Each shape uses a radius r.
activities.explanation: These ideas help you recognise and measure spheres and hemispheres.

activities.prompt: A solid ball is cut through its centre into two equal halves. Compare the new outside area of one half with the ball's old outside area.
steps: The ball is a sphere, so its surface area is 4πr².
The cut makes hemispheres, each with curved area 2πr².
Each hemisphere's circular base adds πr² to its curved area.
Adding them gives 3πr², which is less than 4πr².
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: Find the 3D Shape
activities.prompt: Which shape is the three-dimensional equivalent of a circle?
options: A sphere
A flat disc
A half disc
A cylinder
activities.explanation: Good choice! A sphere is the three-dimensional equivalent of a circle.

activities.title: True or False?
activities.prompt: A hemisphere has one curved surface and one circular base.
activities.explanation: That is correct. A hemisphere has one curved surface and one circular base.

activities.title: Match the Ideas
activities.prompt: Match each description with its shape or formula.
activities.explanation: Each left side matches the shape or formula on the right.

activities.title: Complete the Formula
activities.prompt: The total surface area of a hemisphere is ______.
activities.hint: Use the curved surface area and the circular base area.
activities.explanation: A hemisphere’s total includes its curved surface and circular base. The result is 3πr².

activities.title: Surface Area of a Sphere
activities.prompt: Which expression gives the surface area of a sphere?
options: 3πr²
2πr²
πr²
4πr²
activities.explanation: The surface area of a sphere is 4πr². The hemisphere formulas describe different surfaces.

activities.title: Volume of a Sphere
activities.prompt: Which expression gives the volume of a sphere?
options: Four-thirds of πr³
4πr²
2πr²
πr²
activities.explanation: A sphere’s volume is four-thirds of πr³. The other expressions are surface-area formulas.

activities.title: Make a Hemisphere
activities.prompt: Put these steps in the correct order.
items: Rotate a circle about any diameter.
Cut the sphere through its centre.
Keep one half as a hemisphere.
activities.explanation: Rotation gives a hollow sphere. Cutting through the centre gives equal halves. One half is a hemisphere.

activities.title: Connect Volume and Surface Area
activities.prompt: How can a sphere’s volume be found from its surface area and radius?
options: Entire surface area times the radius
One-third of surface area times radius
Curved surface area times the radius
Circular base area times the radius
activities.explanation: A sphere’s volume equals one-third of its surface area multiplied by its radius. This also equals four-thirds of πr³.

activities.prompt: A sphere and a hemisphere have the same radius. How does the sphere's surface area compare with the hemisphere's curved area?
options: The hemisphere's curved area is twice the sphere's area.
The sphere and hemisphere have the same curved area.
The sphere's area is four times the hemisphere's curved area.
The sphere's area is twice the hemisphere's curved area.

why.The hemisphere's curved area is twice th: This reverses the comparison; the sphere's 4πr² is larger.
why.The sphere and hemisphere have the same: This ignores that 4πr² is larger than 2πr².
why.The sphere's area is four times the hemi: This mistakes the number 4 in one formula for a ratio.

activities.explanation: 4πr² is twice 2πr², so this is correct.

activities.prompt: A sphere is cut into two equal hemispheres. How much volume does one hemisphere have?
options: One hemisphere has twice the sphere's volume.
One hemisphere has half the sphere's volume.
One hemisphere has the sphere's full volume.
One hemisphere has one-third of the sphere's volume.

why.One hemisphere has twice the sphere's vo: One half cannot be larger than the whole sphere.
why.One hemisphere has the sphere's full vol: This treats one half as if it were the whole sphere.
why.One hemisphere has one-third of the sphe: This confuses the one-third rule with the half made by cutting.

activities.title: Estimating volumes
activities.body: Many everyday objects resemble three-dimensional shapes. You can estimate their volumes using suitable measurements. A guesstimate gives a sensible answer when exact information is unavailable. Your final estimate depends on your assumptions and approximations. When estimating tennis balls in a room, gaps matter. Dividing the room’s volume by one ball’s volume gives only an upper bound. Allowing for gaps and using ordered arrangements can provide better estimates.
keyPoints: Volumes can be estimated using suitable measurements.
A guesstimate gives a sensible answer when exact information is unavailable.
Assumptions, approximations and gaps affect the final estimate.
activities.explanation: Good guesstimates explain your thinking clearly.

An upper bound is found by dividing the available volume by the volume of one block.
3600 divided by 100 = 36 blocks.

activities.prompt: Explain the difference between the total surface area and the volume of a cuboid.
activities.answer: Total surface area and volume describe different features of a cuboid. Total surface area measures the whole outer surface, which has six rectangular faces, and is calculated as TSA = 2(wl + hl + hw). Volume measures the space occupied by the cuboid. It is measured in cubic units and is found by multiplying length, width, and height. Another way to understand volume is that it equals the number of unit cubes that fit inside. Therefore, surface area concerns the outer covering, while volume concerns capacity or space.
points: TSA uses all six rectangular faces.
TSA is calculated as 2(wl + hl + hw).
Volume is measured in cubic units.
Volume is length multiplied by width and height.

activities.prompt: Explain how to find the surface area of a closed cylinder and how the result changes if it is closed at only one end.
activities.answer: For a cylinder with radius r and height h, the curved surface area is 2πrh. A closed cylinder has a flat circular surface at each end, and each such surface has area πr², so the total surface area is 2πrh + 2πr². If the cylinder is closed at only one end, one flat circular surface still contributes πr², while the curved surface remains 2πrh. Therefore, the surface area becomes 2πrh + πr², which is smaller by πr² than for the cylinder closed at both ends.

activities.prompt: Explain how the curved surface area of a cone is related to its unrolled surface and why the total surface area is larger.
activities.answer: The unrolled surface of a cone is a sector of a circle. The cone’s curved surface area can be derived by imagining many narrow triangular sectors joined together, and this gives πrl, where l is the slant length and r is the base radius. The total surface area includes both this curved surface and the circular base. The base has area πr², so the total surface area is πrl + πr². Therefore, it is larger than the curved surface area alone by the area of the circular base.

activities.prompt: A sphere is the three-dimensional equivalent of a ______.
activities.hint: Think of a flat round shape.
activities.explanation: A sphere is the three-dimensional equivalent of a circle.

activities.prompt: Match each shape with its surface-area or volume rule.
activities.explanation: Each shape has its own surface-area or volume rule.

activities.title: Closed Cylinder
activities.prompt: Which formula gives the surface area of a cylinder closed at both ends?
options: 2πrh + 2πr²
2πrh + 2πh²
2πrh + 2πr
2πrh + 2πh
activities.explanation: A closed cylinder includes the curved surface and two flat circles.

activities.prompt: The total surface area of a cone is πrl.
activities.explanation: The cone’s total area also includes its circular base.

activities.prompt: The unrolled surface of a cone has the shape of a ______ of a circle.
activities.hint: It is a part of a circle.
activities.explanation: The unrolled surface of a cone is a sector of a circle.

activities.prompt: Put the steps for making a hemisphere in order.
items: Cut a sphere through its centre.
Observe one curved surface and one circular base.
activities.explanation: Cutting through the centre creates two equal halves with one curved surface and one base.

activities.title: Cone and Cylinder
activities.prompt: A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and height. What is the cone’s volume compared with the cylinder’s?
options: one-third
one-half
twice
the same amount
activities.explanation: The cone has one-third of the cylinder’s volume for matching radius and height.

activities.prompt: In a guesstimate, matching another person’s answer matters more than using sound reasoning.
activities.explanation: A good guesstimate explains its assumptions, so your reasoning matters most.
